messages.content: The Denver workshop agenda finally posted. Monday check-in is required by 12:30, so I agree the Monday morning flight is too risky. Can you turn the two hotel holds and the Sunday flight idea into one final plan?

Yes. I would keep the Sunday Jan. 12 arrival and Wednesday Jan. 15 afternoon return. Same-day Monday would leave almost no recovery room for a delay. For flights, the cleanest option I have is Delta Main Cabin nonstop: Sunday SLC to DEN, 3:25 PM to 4:58 PM, and Wednesday DEN to SLC, 3:20 PM to 5:01 PM. Comparable United times are a little later Sunday, and Southwest is fine but does not give an assigned window seat. The Delta fare is about $246 before any bag fee.
Use Delta if it is that close. I will carry on only, and please request window seats where you can.

Done for the flight selection: Delta Main Cabin, carry-on only, window seats requested as 18A outbound and 20F return, subject to aircraft changes. Now the hotel choice is the real trade-off. Official workshop hotel: about $219 per night, above the normal cap, no free breakfast, but the meeting is in the building and dinner is easy on-site. Hampton Inn & Suites Downtown/Convention Center: about $181 per night, breakfast included, refundable queen room, but it is about a 10 to 12 minute walk to the workshop hotel.

I wanted the breakfast, but January walking in downtown Denver with a laptop and materials is not worth saving thirty-something dollars a night. If the conference-rate note covers it, choose the official hotel.

That is the more reliable workshop plan. I will keep the official hotel block, standard queen, non-smoking, Jan. 12 to Jan. 15, and release the Hampton hold before its cancellation deadline. Breakfast is not included, but the hotel cafe opens early enough for Monday and Tuesday, and the on-site restaurant plus nearby 16th Street options cover dinner.
Please make sure the room is refundable and that they know I may arrive around 6:30 Sunday.

Confirmed into the notes: refundable conference block, standard queen, non-smoking, late arrival around 6:30 PM Sunday. The cancellation deadline remains Jan. 9 at 6:00 PM. The room rate is above the normal nightly cap, so I would attach a short justification to the reimbursement pre-approval.
Yes, draft that note. Also ground transportation: no rental, right?

No rental needed. Best plan is the A Line from DEN to Union Station, then a short rideshare to the hotel if the sidewalks are snowy or you have the materials bag. If the flight is delayed or weather is bad, take a rideshare straight from the airport and save the receipt. Expected costs: train about $10 to $11, short rideshare about $10 to $15, or full airport rideshare often $55 to $75.
Good. I need the final version I can send my director, including the reimbursement wording.

Here is the director-ready version: I recommend flying Sunday afternoon rather than Monday morning because the workshop requires in-person check-in by 12:30 PM Monday, and January weather makes a same-day arrival unreliable. Selected flights are Delta Main Cabin nonstop SLC-DEN Sunday Jan. 12, 3:25 PM to 4:58 PM, and DEN-SLC Wednesday Jan. 15, 3:20 PM to 5:01 PM, carry-on only, window seats requested. I recommend the official workshop hotel for Jan. 12 to Jan. 15 because it eliminates weather-related walking between hotels and keeps me on-site for required sessions. The conference block rate is above the standard nightly cap, so I am requesting approval to reimburse the official conference rate due to mandatory workshop attendance, winter travel reliability, and lack of transportation cost while on site. No rental car is planned; I will use airport rail or rideshare and submit receipts.
That works. Release the Hampton and keep the official block. Send me a final checklist after that.

Final Denver checklist: Hampton hold released; official workshop hotel kept for Jan. 12 to Jan. 15, refundable standard queen, late-arrival note added, cancellation deadline Jan. 9 at 6:00 PM. Flights selected: Delta nonstop SLC-DEN Sunday afternoon and DEN-SLC Wednesday afternoon, carry-on only, window seats requested. Ground transport: A Line plus short rideshare unless weather or delays make a direct rideshare smarter. Food: hotel cafe for breakfast at personal/work per diem, on-site or nearby restaurants for dinner. Reimbursement note is ready to attach for the above-cap conference hotel rate.

messages.content: Quick Denver check. Delta shifted the Sunday outbound by 18 minutes later, and now there is a Front Range storm forecast Sunday night. I do not want to rebuild the trip, just tell me if I should move earlier.

With the shift, you are still arriving before the worst part of the forecast if the current timing holds. I would keep the flight unless the storm timing moves into Sunday afternoon. The earlier noon-ish option buys more buffer, but it also turns this into a much longer travel day for a risk that is still mostly evening and overnight.
So keep the shifted flight for now?

Yes. Keep it, check the airline app Saturday evening and Sunday morning, and only move earlier if Delta issues a waiver or the forecast starts showing snow at DEN before 5 PM. For your current flight, plan to be inside SLC by 1:35 PM. Leave home or campus by 12:50 PM, 12:40 if roads are wet.
The hotel confirmed breakfast starts at 6:30. Their restaurant closes early Sunday, though. Badge pickup is digital but available in the lobby Monday morning.

That works. Sunday dinner plan: if you land on time, take the A Line to Union Station and grab something there before the short rideshare to the hotel. If the flight is late, buy a sandwich or bowl at DEN before leaving the secure side. Do not count on the hotel restaurant after about 7 PM.
Rail still better than rideshare from the airport in this weather?

Use rail unless the A Line is disrupted. It is less exposed to highway traffic and surge pricing. Then take a short rideshare from Union Station to the hotel rather than walking with luggage in snow. Save both receipts.
Can you give me the tiny final checklist, including receipts?

Denver final checklist: keep shifted Sunday Delta flight; leave by 12:40 to 12:50 PM and be at SLC by 1:35 PM; carry on only; check app Saturday night and Sunday morning for waiver or storm timing; use A Line to Union Station plus short rideshare unless rail is disrupted; dinner at Union Station or DEN if delayed; Monday breakfast starts 6:30; digital badge pickup Monday morning before 12:30 check-in. Receipt folder: airfare confirmation, hotel folio, airport rail, rideshares, meals under per diem, and the above-cap hotel approval note. Pack: laptop and charger, workshop agenda, badge QR code, admissions materials, winter coat, gloves, walking shoes, and one compact umbrella.

messages.content: Denver is wrapped, and now Idaho landed on my desk. Late February swing: Tuesday evening admitted-student reception in Boise, Wednesday 7:30 AM counselor breakfast in Nampa, Wednesday afternoon transfer table in Twin Falls, and Thursday morning high-school visit near Pocatello. I need to compare full drive, Boise round-trip, and open-jaw with a rental car.
I can make that practical. One question before I rank them: how much material are you carrying, and do you need to be home Thursday night?

Two medium boxes, tablecloth, retractable banner, laptop bag. I can ship one box to Boise if that makes flying workable. I would strongly prefer to be home Thursday by dinner, but not at the cost of a sketchy connection or a 5 AM road start.

Here is the short version. Full drive from Salt Lake City: easiest for materials and cheapest to approve, but it puts all winter-road risk on I-84/I-86 and is about 620 to 650 miles total. Boise round-trip flight: convenient outbound, but after Pocatello you would backtrack several hours to Boise, so I would not recommend it unless airfare is dramatically cheaper. Open-jaw: fly SLC to Boise, rent one-way, drive Boise to Nampa to Twin Falls to Pocatello, then return from Idaho Falls to SLC. That is the best schedule fit if the one-way rental fee is reasonable and you ship or consolidate materials.
Open-jaw sounds best, but I do not want some weird two-stop return from Idaho Falls.

I would avoid that too. Idaho Falls to Salt Lake City usually has a short nonstop on Delta/SkyWest, and that is the return to check first. Pocatello airport is closer but has thinner schedules, so Idaho Falls is the safer return airport. Boise to Salt Lake City also has nonstops, so the open-jaw can be two simple flight legs with no connection.
Okay, use Idaho Falls for the return comparison. What does the overnight sequence look like?

Recommended sequence: Tuesday fly or drive into Boise, handle the evening reception, then sleep in Meridian or Nampa so the 7:30 AM breakfast is easy. Wednesday after breakfast, drive to Twin Falls for the transfer table. After that, drive on to Pocatello and sleep there Wednesday night. Thursday do the high-school visit, then drive about 50 minutes to Idaho Falls for the return flight.
Would it be safer to sleep in Twin Falls Wednesday and drive to Pocatello Thursday morning?

For a Thursday morning school visit, I would not. Twin Falls to Pocatello is roughly two hours in good conditions, and a winter delay Thursday morning could jeopardize the visit. Driving Twin Falls to Pocatello Wednesday late afternoon gives you more recovery room. If the Twin Falls event ends after dark or the forecast is ugly, then the backup is to ask the Pocatello school for a later Thursday visit, not to gamble on a predawn drive.
That makes sense. Give me hotel areas with breakfast, parking, and dinner nearby. Nothing fancy.

For Tuesday night, look at Nampa near the Civic Center or Idaho Center, or west Meridian if rates are better. Those areas usually have free parking, breakfast-included brands, and easy chain restaurants. Downtown Boise is better for dinner but worse for the 7:30 Nampa start. For Wednesday night, use Pocatello along I-15/Bench Road or near the ISU/Yield area depending on the school address; both have free parking and quick dinner options on Yellowstone Avenue. For Twin Falls, you may not need an overnight, but Blue Lakes Boulevard is the best backup area if roads force a stop.
I have campus meetings until 11 Tuesday if I keep them. Is an afternoon flight to Boise too tight for a 6 PM reception?

It depends on how much setup the reception needs. A 1:30 or 2:00 PM SLC departure could work if it is nonstop and on time, but it leaves less room for rental-car pickup, weather, and material wrangling. For reliability, I would target a late-morning or noon nonstop to Boise and hand off the 11 AM meeting if you can.
Protect the reception. I can hand off the 11 AM meeting. If the flight is around noon, I am fine.

Then the open-jaw plan becomes stronger: noon-ish SLC to Boise on Tuesday, one-way rental at BOI, Nampa/Meridian hotel Tuesday night, Twin Falls Wednesday afternoon, Pocatello hotel Wednesday night, and Thursday return from Idaho Falls after the school visit. For the return, I would look for mid- to late-afternoon out of IDA so you are not rushing from Pocatello.
What do we need to flag before I ask for approval?

Four items: airfare, one-way rental fee, winter-road exposure, and materials handling. For airfare, compare SLC-BOI plus IDA-SLC against round-trip Boise and against mileage reimbursement for full drive. For the rental, confirm the one-way drop fee and that a compact SUV or midsize can hold the banner and boxes. For weather, note that open-jaw reduces total driving but does not eliminate I-84/I-86 exposure. For materials, ship one box to the Boise reception site if they can receive it, and carry the banner plus one box in the rental.
If my director vetoes the one-way rental drop fee, what is the fallback?

Fallback should be full drive, not Boise round-trip flying. Drive SLC to Boise Tuesday with an earlier start, overnight Nampa/Meridian, drive Nampa to Twin Falls to Pocatello Wednesday, then Pocatello to SLC after the Thursday school visit. It is longer behind the wheel, but it keeps materials simple and avoids the Boise backtrack after Pocatello. Add a weather check 48 hours out and permission to leave Monday evening or ship materials if I-84 looks bad.
Please make that into a short attachment for approval. Do not book yet.

Approval draft: Recommended plan is open-jaw air plus one-way rental for the late-February Idaho yield swing. Fly SLC to Boise around noon Tuesday, rent a car at BOI, attend the Boise evening reception, and stay Tuesday night in Nampa or west Meridian for the Wednesday 7:30 AM counselor breakfast. Continue Wednesday to the Twin Falls transfer table, then drive to Pocatello Wednesday evening and stay near I-15/Bench Road or ISU for the Thursday morning high-school visit. Return Thursday from Idaho Falls to Salt Lake City on a mid- or late-afternoon nonstop if available. Hotels should include parking and breakfast, with nearby dinner options. Items to price before approval: open-jaw airfare, one-way rental/drop fee, full-drive mileage comparison, and cost or feasibility of shipping one materials box to Boise. Backup if one-way rental is denied: full drive from Salt Lake City with the same Nampa/Meridian and Pocatello overnights; avoid Boise round-trip flying because it creates a long backtrack after Pocatello.
